title: Greenhouse Effect & Temperature Regulation

competencies.text: Describe how the greenhouse effect regulates Earth's temperature.

days.title: Earth's Energy Balance
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will describe how the greenhouse effect regulates Earth's temperature.

☀️ Energy In, Energy Out

Earth's temperature stays fairly stable because the energy it receives from the Sun is balanced by the energy it sends back to space.

  • About 30% of incoming sunlight is reflected by clouds, ice and bright surfaces. This reflectivity is called albedo.
  • About 20% is absorbed by the atmosphere.
  • About 50% is absorbed by land and oceans, warming them.

🔁 Short Waves In, Long Waves Out

Sunlight arrives mostly as visible light (short wavelength), which passes easily through the air. The warmed surface then gives off infrared radiation (heat, longer wavelength). Some gases in the air absorb this infrared and send part of it back down. If incoming and outgoing energy are equal, the average temperature stays steady. If more energy is trapped than leaves, Earth warms.

🧊 Albedo Matters

Bright ice and snow reflect most sunlight; dark oceans and forests absorb most of it. When ice melts, darker surfaces are exposed, more sunlight is absorbed, and warming speeds up — a feedback loop.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

choices.label: The fraction of sunlight a surface reflects
The amount of CO₂ stored in the deep oceans
The speed at which the Earth rotates
The heat produced by Earth's core

scenario.explanation: Albedo measures reflectivity: ice has a high albedo, oceans and forests have a low albedo.

scenario.text: In what form does Earth's warm surface give off energy?

choices.label: Infrared radiation
Ultraviolet rays
Visible blue light
Sound waves

scenario.explanation: Warm objects radiate heat as infrared, which greenhouse gases can absorb.

scenario.text: As polar ice melts, more dark ocean is exposed. What happens next?

choices.label: More sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming
More sunlight is reflected, causing global cooling
Nothing changes because water is colorless
The ocean freezes again within a few days

scenario.explanation: Dark water has a lower albedo than ice, so it absorbs more energy — a feedback that speeds up warming.

days.title: Greenhouse Gases
days.content:
🌿 The Natural Greenhouse Effect

Certain gases absorb infrared radiation and re-emit it in all directions, including back to the surface. Without this effect, Earth's average temperature would be about −18 °C instead of about 15 °C — too cold for most life.

GasMain sourcesNote
Water vapor (H₂O)EvaporationMost abundant; increases as air warms
Carbon dioxide (CO₂)Burning fossil fuels, deforestationMain driver of recent warming; stays for centuries
Methane (CH₄)Livestock, rice paddies, landfillsAbout 28 times stronger than CO₂ over 100 years
Nitrous oxide (N₂O)Nitrogen fertilizersAbout 265 times stronger than CO₂
Fluorinated gasesOld refrigerants and aircon leaksCan be thousands of times stronger

🔥 Natural vs Enhanced

The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth habitable. The enhanced greenhouse effect is the extra warming from greenhouse gases added by human activities since the Industrial Revolution. Atmospheric CO₂ has risen from about 280 ppm before 1800 to more than 420 ppm today.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Gases trap infrared heat and warm the surface
Released by fossil fuels and deforestation
From livestock, rice paddies and landfills

match.why: It increases as air gets warmer.

match.right: Heat given off by Earth's surface

days.title: When the Balance Shifts
days.content:
📈 More Gas, More Heat

When greenhouse gases increase, less infrared escapes to space. Earth gains more energy than it loses until the surface warms enough to restore balance at a higher temperature. The global average has already risen about 1.1–1.2 °C since the late 1800s.

🔄 Feedback Loops

FeedbackHow it worksEffect
Ice–albedoWarming melts ice → darker surface absorbs more sunlightMore warming
Water vaporWarmer air holds more water vapor, a greenhouse gasMore warming
PermafrostThawing frozen soil releases methane and CO₂More warming
Plant growthMore CO₂ can increase photosynthesis in some plantsSlight cooling (limited)

🇵🇭 Fairness and Responsibility

The Philippines produces only a small share of global emissions (well under 1%) but faces stronger typhoons, sea-level rise and heat. Climate change is global: gases from anywhere warm the whole planet. Every country, including ours, can reduce emissions and prepare for impacts.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Apply the greenhouse model. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: Sunlight passes easily through the atmosphere, but heat from the ground does not escape as easily. Why?

choices.label: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared but pass visible light
Clouds block every kind of radiation in both directions equally
The ground absorbs all heat and never releases it
Visible light turns into ice when it hits the ground

scenario.explanation: Incoming sunlight is mostly visible light, which passes through. Outgoing heat is infrared, which greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit.

scenario.text: A large livestock farm produces a lot of methane. Why does this matter for climate?

choices.label: Methane traps more heat per molecule than CO₂
Methane cools the air by blocking sunlight
Methane removes ozone, which cools the whole Earth
Methane turns into oxygen in a few minutes

scenario.explanation: Methane is a strong greenhouse gas — about 28 times as effective as CO₂ over 100 years.

scenario.text: Without the natural greenhouse effect, what would Earth's average temperature be?

choices.label: About −18 °C
About 15 °C
About 33 °C
About 100 °C

scenario.explanation: Greenhouse gases keep Earth roughly 33 °C warmer than it would otherwise be (about 15 °C instead of −18 °C).

scenario.text: A student says, "Since the greenhouse effect is natural, adding more CO₂ cannot cause harm." Which response is BEST?

choices.label: Extra CO₂ strengthens the effect beyond natural levels
The student is right; natural things never cause any harm
CO₂ has no effect on temperature at any amount
The greenhouse effect only happens on Venus, not Earth

scenario.explanation: The natural effect is helpful, but adding more greenhouse gases traps extra heat and raises the temperature — the enhanced effect.

scenario.text: Why is warmer air holding more water vapor a concern?

choices.label: Water vapor is also a greenhouse gas
Water vapor reflects all sunlight back to space
Water vapor removes carbon dioxide from the air
Water vapor makes the air much colder at night

scenario.explanation: This is a positive feedback: warming adds water vapor, and more water vapor traps more heat.

days.title: Reducing Our Greenhouse Footprint
days.content:
🏠 Everyday Choices

  • Save electricity: much of our power comes from coal. Turning off unused lights and choosing efficient appliances reduces CO₂.
  • Walk, bike or take public transport instead of private cars for short trips.
  • Reduce food waste and compost: rotting food in dumpsites releases methane.
  • Maintain aircons and refrigerators to prevent leaks of strong fluorinated gases.
  • Plant and protect trees and mangroves, which absorb CO₂.

🇵🇭 National Efforts

The Philippines has committed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions under the Paris Agreement and is expanding renewable energy — geothermal (we are among the world's top geothermal producers), hydro, solar and wind. Rice farmers are trying alternate wetting and drying, which reduces methane from paddies.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: Which greenhouse gas is MOST abundant naturally in the atmosphere?

choices.label: Water vapor
Carbon dioxide
Methane gas
Nitrous oxide

escape.explanation: Water vapor is the most abundant greenhouse gas, though its amount depends on temperature.

escape.text: What type of radiation do greenhouse gases absorb?

choices.label: Infrared
Ultraviolet
X-rays
Gamma rays

escape.explanation: Greenhouse gases absorb the infrared (heat) radiation given off by Earth's surface.

escape.text: What is the ENHANCED greenhouse effect caused by?

choices.label: Greenhouse gases added by human activities
Natural water vapor from the oceans only, every year
The Sun moving closer to the Earth
The ozone layer becoming much thicker

escape.explanation: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation and agriculture add extra gases, strengthening the natural effect.

escape.text: Which rice-farming practice reduces methane emissions?

choices.label: Alternate wetting and drying of fields
Keeping fields flooded all year long
Burning the rice straw in the field
Using more nitrogen fertilizer each time

escape.explanation: Methane forms in flooded, oxygen-poor soil. Letting fields dry out periodically reduces methane.

escape.text: Which planet shows a runaway greenhouse effect?

choices.label: Venus
Mars
Mercury
Earth

escape.explanation: Venus' thick CO₂ atmosphere traps so much heat that its surface is hotter than Mercury's.

escape.text: Which household action BEST reduces greenhouse gas emissions?

choices.label: Switching to efficient LEDs and appliances
Leaving the TV on standby mode all day
Burning dry leaves and plastic in the yard
Throwing all food scraps into the open dumpsite

escape.explanation: Efficient appliances use less electricity, much of which comes from burning fossil fuels.
